subject: Repo-agnostic Claude Code workflow skills with template config
body:
A set of Claude Code skills for structured feature development:
- review-goals: Review goals documents for gaps and risks
- create-html-mock: Create and iterate on HTML mocks
- extract-requirements-from-mock: Extract requirements from mock sessions
- write-requirements: Generate requirements from goals via Q&A
- write-architecture: Design architecture from goals and requirements
- write-implementation-plan: Create fine-grained, self-contained task files
- execute-implementation-plan: Execute task files with verification at each step
- fix-bug: TDD bug fix workflow with regression testing

All skills reference a central workflow-config.md template with placeholders
for project-specific paths, commands, test conventions, and related skills.
Skills use "end-to-end test" terminology throughout.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P0-#2: Bind task file path in implement_task.md
body:
implement_task.md referenced $TASK_FILE with no binding. Rewrite to take
the task path from the current TODO entry passed by the executor: add a
"subject task file" preamble defining the binding, and replace the
remaining $TASK_FILE reference with prose pointing at the dequeued path.
This preserves the author's structure (separate file from the executor)
while removing the broken variable.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P0-#3: Create implementation_plan/ folder before writing into it
body:
write-implementation-plan step 4 wrote _exploration_notes.md into
implementation_plan/ before that folder existed (it was created
implicitly by the Output Structure later). Add an explicit
"create the implementation_plan/ folder" step before the exploration
notes step so creation order is correct, and renumber the later steps.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P0-#4: Unify requirements.md shape across both authoring paths
body:
extract-requirements-from-mock and write-requirements produced
incompatible requirements.md formats, but write-architecture consumes
either one and assumes a single shape. Adopt the write-requirements
shape in extract-requirements-from-mock: REQ-<CATEGORY>-<N> IDs,
MUST/SHOULD/MAY language, an Out of Scope section, and an acceptance
criteria summary table. Mock-extraction guidance ("focus on user-facing
behavior, no implementation details") is preserved.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P1-#5: Document interactivity expectations in the README
body:
The README pitches overnight autonomous coding, but several skills hard-
block on user confirmation (fix-bug Phase 1 mandatorily stops; create-
html-mock asks for a feature name; the writers ask clarifying questions
before producing artifacts). Add an "Interactivity" section calling out
which skills require human input vs. which are safe to run unattended,
so users can plan accordingly without changing skill behavior.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P1-#6: Add machine-readable tasks YAML block to 00_overview.md
body:
execute-implementation-plan parsed the human-readable Task Index table
to build its TODO list, which made the executor brittle to any drift in
table formatting. Add a tasks: YAML block to the 00_overview.md template
alongside the table, mark it as the source of truth, and have the
executor parse the YAML instead. Keep the table for humans.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P1-#7: Triage failures instead of treating all as the agent's bug
body:
implement_task.md previously declared "ALL failures are your
responsibility" with no escape hatch, which caused scope creep on long
autonomous runs (the agent would chase unrelated, pre-existing bugs).
Soften the rule: if a failure is caused by the agent's change, fix it;
if it already exists on the base branch (verified with `git stash` or
HEAD~1), report it as a blocker and stop. The default assumption is
still that the failure is the agent's to fix — verification is required
before treating it as pre-existing.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P2-#8: Move workflow-config.md out of the skills directory
body:
.claude/skills/ is conventionally for skill folders only, but the
workflow-config template lived alongside them as a stray file. Move it
to .claude/workflow-config.md and update every reference across the
eight SKILL.md files, implement_task.md, and the Setup line inside the
config itself.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P2-#9: Allow lists of commands for FORMAT/CHECK/UNIT_TEST slots
body:
Real projects often have multi-step quality pipelines (build → lint →
test, sometimes per package). Document that the FORMAT_COMMAND,
CHECK_COMMAND, and UNIT_TEST_COMMAND slots accept either a single
command or a list, with examples for both shapes; the consuming skills
(implement_task.md and fix-bug Phase 3) now run a list in order and
stop at the first failure.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P2-#10: Add UI_CODE_ROOT slot to workflow-config.md
body:
create-html-mock told the agent to "read the UI code" without giving a
hint where it lives. Add a <UI_CODE_ROOT> placeholder to the Product
identity section of workflow-config.md (with example values), and point
create-html-mock step 5 at that slot. The whole Product identity section
is still optional — backend-only projects delete it.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P2-#11: Standardize argument-hint syntax across all skills
body:
Conventions: <…> for required arguments, [...] for optional, kebab-case
for the placeholder. Apply consistently:

- create-html-mock: [feature description] → [feature-description] (still
  optional; the skill can ask the user if not provided).
- extract-requirements-from-mock: [feature-name] → <feature-name> (the
  skill needs the name to find the feature folder; not optional).
- fix-bug: missing argument-hint → [bug-description] (optional; the
  skill asks clarifying questions when the description is vague).

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: P2-#12: Handle empty conversation history in extract-requirements-from-mock
body:
Step 2 told the agent to "review the conversation history for any
additional context", but that history is empty when the skill is invoked
in a fresh session — the user could have iterated on mocks days earlier.
Add a note that, when no prior context exists, the agent should rely
solely on the durable record in mocks.context.md and mocks.html.

subject: Add /setup-workflow skill
body:
Walks the user through .claude/workflow-config.md and replaces
<PLACEHOLDER> values interactively. Offers an optional Backlog section

when the config is missing or unfilled.

subject: Add /next orchestrator skill
body:
The single entry point to start or continue feature work. Reads
.claude/workflow-config.md, finds or selects the active feature, and
either runs or just describes the next slash command in the workflow.

Behavior:
- /next       — run the next command for the active feature
- /next ?     — describe the next command without running it
- /next text  — start a new feature seeded with that description
                (auto-routes to /fix-bug for bug-shaped descriptions)

Stage detection by artifact presence; staleness check by mtime.
Workspace-local active-feature pointer at <docs-directory>/.next-current,
gitignored. README adds a Tip pointing to /next and /setup-workflow,
and lists both as interactive skills.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

body:

subject: Add shared interaction conventions for workflow skills
body:
Introduces .claude/skills/_shared/interaction.md as a single source of truth
for how workflow skills should talk to the user: terse-vs-verbose mode,
small-chunk question pacing, and a numbered-question / lettered-option format
that lets the user reply with compact answers like "1a,2c".

- New _shared/interaction.md with the conventions
- workflow-config.md template gains an "Interaction style" section with a
  normal/expert verbosity setting; /setup-workflow asks for it during setup
- Every workflow skill now points at the shared file near its top, so the
  rules are picked up without duplicating prose in each skill

subject: Tighten autonomy rules for plan write/execute skills
body:
Three connected changes so /write-implementation-plan and
/execute-implementation-plan run longer without stopping for user input:

- write-implementation-plan: every task must end green. Plans that require
  a red intermediate state (one task breaks the build, a later task fixes
  it) are now explicitly a planning bug — use expand-contract or bundling
  instead. Clarifying questions are batched into a single round and only
  asked when defaults can't be inferred from workflow-config.md or code.
- execute-implementation-plan: explicit stopping rules. Stop only on real
  blockers (verification failure outside this task's scope, missing API,
  genuine ambiguity). Do not stop to confirm between green tasks or to
  resolve a "task notes vs skill defaults" conflict — task notes never
  override safety/verification rules; a conflicting task is a planning
  bug to surface, not a question to ask.
- implement_task.md: format/lint/trivial type errors are auto-fixed and
  retried; blockers are surfaced only when truly outside task scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: Add recommendation convention to shared interaction conventions
body:
Skills end each question turn with a "Recommend: ..." line so the user
can accept the model's read in one reply. Expert mode = single-line
recommendation only; normal mode = one line per answer with a brief
reason. Skip only when genuinely no preference is possible.

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: Move language-specific code rules out of implement_task.md
body:
The implementer step in implement_task.md hardcoded three Python-style
rules: top-of-file imports, no relative imports, and no docstrings.
These are project/language conventions, not workflow rules, so they
violated the "skills agnostic, project specifics in workflow-config"
split.

- implement_task.md: drop the import/docstring rules. Keep the universal
  "no unnecessary comments or abstractions". Keep the type-hint rule but
  gate it on "if the language supports them". Add a pointer to the new
  Code conventions section in workflow-config.md.
- workflow-config.md: add an optional Code conventions section so
  Python/TS/etc. projects can paste in their repo-wide rules.
- setup-workflow: list Code conventions as an optional section to
  walk through (or skip + delete).

Co-authored-by: Sculptor <sculptor@imbue.com>

subject: Restructure as mise plugin and simplify the state engine
body:
Plugin restructure: the old .claude/skills/* set becomes a single
user-invoked skill (skills/next) with stages/, references/, and a
TypeScript state engine; docs consolidate into README + skill-authoring
guide + the engine spec (docs/state-machine.md).

State engine redesign — two commands (report, approve), three ideas:

- Task completion lives in the filesystem: finished task files move to
  implementation_plan/done/, scoped to one approved plan version — a
  plan approval whose hash doesn't match the recorded one clears it.
  tasks_done, set, reopen, and the stale-task gate are gone.
- The route rides on the goals approval (approve goals route=...), so a
  goals approval without a route is unrepresentable; route_lost and the
  approve-mock side effect are gone.
- No recovery by inference: a broken or unexpectedly missing state file
  is an error naming the user's options (restore from the last mise:
  checkpoint, or delete the mise directory and start over); the
  salvage/inference tier and orphan_task_files are gone.

Execute stage: baseline gate scoped to the plan's first task (mid-plan
red is the work's to fix, never "pre-existing"); a stuck implementer
gets one fresh-context retry, a blocked one stops immediately.

Instruction files trimmed so every rule has one home; setup commits the
generated config; no-e2e projects get a blanket Test exception at setup.

subject: Mock IDs, mental-model audit, and New Concepts section
body:
Each mock now carries a unique ID as the handle for feedback, the mock
step audits new UI concepts against the user's mental model, and
mocks.context.md records surviving concepts (with why no existing
concept fits) for the user to veto at the gate. The requirements critic
checks the section for traceability. Bump to 1.2.0.

subject: Require a branch convention and create work branches at start
body:
Starting new work now ensures a work branch: on the default branch it
creates one from the config's new required Branch convention value; on
any other branch it asks whether to reuse it. Missing convention
re-fires the config gate. Bump to 1.3.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Add a Kaizen retrospective to the close-out
body:
After acceptance confirmation and before cleanup, a fresh-context
retrospective subagent mines the run for guidance improvements and
proposes minimal edits routed to their natural home: an existing
guide, the config, CLAUDE.md, a new registered doc (only when
critical), or a report-only plugin candidate — anything else is
dropped. The user adopts or rejects each proposal by number; adopted
edits land as one ordinary commit, and rejecting everything never
blocks finishing.

Raw material comes from a new friction log (_friction.md): critic
gates record multi-round passes and stalls, execute records task
failures, reviewer defects, and acceptance items the user flags.
Only the retrospective reads it, so it costs later stages nothing.

No state-engine changes: the retrospective rides the acceptance
tail, and an interrupted close-out re-reports acceptance as before.
Opt out with a top-level `Retrospective: off` config line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Add ship step, CLAUDE.md ship guard, and recorded acceptance close-out
body:
Shipping is now part of the pipeline: after the cleanup commit the
close-out ships per the config's Ship value (pr | merge (<style>) | off,
asked at setup; the merge style is a recorded choice, never assumed).
Setup also writes a CLAUDE.md guard so sessions outside the workflow
refuse to PR/merge any branch whose tree still contains the mise
directory.

The state engine records the user's acceptance confirmation as an
`accepted` hash (every route stage's artifact plus the sorted done/
listing) via `approve <dir> acceptance`; report returns `close_out`
while the record matches, so an interrupted close-out resumes at the
retrospective instead of re-running the pass. The record is deleted
whenever a report observes a doc mismatch or an approval records a
changed hash, so a byte-identical revert can never resurrect an
acceptance for re-executed work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Add configurable model delegation for workflow subagents
body:
An optional ## Models section in .claude/mise-config.md maps subagent
roles (implementer, reviewer, critic, acceptance, explore, retrospective)
to models; dispatch sites pass the assigned model to the Agent call while
unassigned roles inherit the session model. Setup interviews for it,
suggesting generation roles on opus with quality gates on the session
model.

subject: Task 1.1: Replace the critic gate's blocking-count stall rule with convergence tracking
body:
Points 3 and 4 of "The critic gate" in skills/next/references/interaction.md
now decide continuation by defect identity instead of blocking counts, which
misfired whenever a round of all-new findings matched or exceeded the previous
round's count even though every prior fix had landed.

Point 3 (nested conditional bullets, per docs/skill-authoring.md):
- classify each blocking finding against all prior rounds in the loop as
  recurring or fresh, which is what catches A -> B -> A ping-pong;
- an all-fresh round continues; the loop's first recurrence event earns one
  more fix attempt, with stall triggers taking precedence over that retry;
- exactly three stall triggers: third sighting, ping-pong (a second recurrence
  event on a different blocker), and budget exhausted;
- round budget of 5 rounds per artifact version with no complexity scaling; a
  substantial scope-change rewrite resets budget, recurrence memory, and the
  recurrence-event count; an absolute ceiling of 8 rounds bounds the unattended
  loop, while a user-directed post-stall round may exceed it and keeps the
  loop's memory;
- one friction line per recurrence event as it happens.

Point 4 presents the artifact and per-round counts as history, labels each
remaining blocker recurring or fresh as the user's decision signal, and names
the trigger that fired; the stall friction line becomes
`critic <stage>: stalled (<trigger>) after <N> rounds`.

Points 1, 2, 5, 6 and "The friction log" are unchanged, and neither stage file
was touched -- the gate is defined once and referenced.

Verified per the config's instruction-file test exception: format, typecheck,
and the 42 unit tests pass, plus a dry-run walkthrough of all four REQ-VERIFY-1
scenarios recorded in the progress log.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Task 1.2: Sync the README's critic-loop stall annotation to the new rule
body:
The ASCII workflow diagram annotated the critic gate's stall as
"(stall: no progress / 5 rounds)" — the count-comparison rule task 1.1
removed from skills/next/references/interaction.md. It now reads
"(stall: recurring blockers / round budget)", using that file's exact
terms: the loop stalls on defects that keep coming back, or on the round
budget running out, not on a round failing to reduce a blocking count.

The full rule (the third sighting / ping-pong / budget exhausted
triggers, the recurrence-event retry, the absolute ceiling) stays in the
skill file; the README describes the loop at annotation depth only.

Scanned the rest of README.md for other statements of the old behavior —
no further hits, so the numbered stage list is unchanged. Diagram column
bars still align at columns 25 and 61 across the fenced block.

subject: Replace count-based critic-gate stall rule with convergence tracking
body:
The critic loop now classifies each round's blocking findings as fresh or
recurring against all prior rounds: all-fresh rounds continue, the loop's
first recurrence gets one retry, and it stalls only on a recurrence
pattern (third sighting or ping-pong) or the round budget (5 per artifact
version, scope-rewrite reset, 8 absolute). Stall messages label blockers
recurring/fresh and name the fired trigger. README synced; version bumped
to 1.7.0; retrospective learnings adopted.

subject: Task 1.1: Revise the skill authoring guide to the v2 writing bar
body:
Rewrites docs/skill-authoring.md so every later v2 task writes against the
shorter bar: as short as possible, rationale only where a rule would
otherwise be misapplied, and the "would removing this line cause a mistake?"
test.

- Deleted "Do not terse-ify them into summary bullets" from "Match
  specificity to fragility"; it contradicted the new length bar.
- Replaced "Every rule carries one clause of why" with "Rationale only where
  a rule would otherwise be misapplied".
- Reworded "The removal test" to Anthropic's per-line phrasing and added the
  smallest-set-of-high-signal-lines principle; its example is now the config
  gate, since v2 removes the `?` explain mode.
- Replaced the `/mise:next ?` example under "Validate edits against real
  runs" with `/mise:next` on a throwaway branch or a dry-run walkthrough.
- Refreshed the snapshot to August 2026 after re-reading both linked sources
  plus the Claude Code best-practices and memory docs, folding in the
  length/adherence evidence, the reviewer-scope caveat, the PR-size data
  (84% of >1000-line diffs draw findings vs 31% under 50) behind the

subject: Task 1.2: Define the v2 config surface in the config reference
body:
`references/config-reference.md` now documents every v2 config value and
section, in both its generated-file example and its section reference:

- `Checklist:` — a required top-level value naming the project's review
  checklist file, with that file's shape (`# Review checklist`, `## Code`
  then `## Prose`, rules numbered continuously, `<rule> — <how to check>`,
  each answerable pass / fail / n-a), the 15-rule cap that never blocks, and
  the rule that a missing value or a missing file is unfilled and blocks the
  execute stage while setup re-creates the starter file.
- `Task tests:` — an optional fourth Quality commands slot whose `<path>`
  placeholder per-task verification fills with the task's tests or touched
  directories, falling back to `Unit tests`; full `Unit tests` always runs at
  the end-of-plan gate.
- `## Review notes` — an optional freeform section read verbatim like
  `## Backlog`, naming the branch's external review notes source.

  two-pass mode on, so setup writes `documenter: session` explicitly, the one
  exception to the omit-`session` rule.

Every entry was tightened to one sentence of meaning and one of format, and
consumption rules stated where they are consumed were dropped, taking the
file to 930 words against a 750 target (the overage and each cut are recorded
in the progress log).

subject: Task 1.3 fix: restore the critic's e2e and file-reference checks, add the dispatch template
body:
roles/critic.md

  covers and no Test exception excuses; a unit test the task writes does not

subject: Task 3.2: rewrite stages/plan.md with the task-size guardrail and the v2 templates

lists at most 5 source files (tests, snapshots, and fixtures don't count; every

Per-task verification is rescoped to what a task can run on its own: the task
template's checklist ends with "Tests: <unit tests to run / tests this task
writes / or the cited Test exception and its substitute verification>" in place

"Include validation in every file" name the same three kinds, and pre-existing
e2e and sanity suites are named only by the overview's new "## End-of-plan gate"
section, which the overview template now carries after Phase Rationale. The
e2e-mandatory principle stays, satisfied by that gate plus the e2e tests tasks
write and run themselves.

The critic step is one line naming kind and upstream; its check list lives in
roles/critic.md. The bugfix route, the seven feature-route steps, both fenced
templates and every field name downstream roles read are unchanged in substance.

subject: Task 1.1: rescope the documenter, slim the progress log, de-duplicate the checklist
body:
Four coupled changes across the six instruction files that define the execute
stage's behavior.

1. Checklist evidence moves out of the progress log. The implementer's log entry
   keeps Key changes and Deviations, bounded to one line each with the detail
   directed to the commit body; the `Checklist:` answers and the "every rule
   number appears exactly once" rule move into the commit template. The
   documenter's step 7 takes the same move, and its entry heading gains the task
   ID.

2. The documenter is rescoped from the branch to one commit set. It now mirrors
   the implementer's three dispatch shapes — task, task fix, and `Fix scope:` —
   each fixing one of three progress-log headings and binding the four sites
   where a prose pass is owed. Scope resolves from the dispatch's `Commits:`; on
   a defect round with no new commit, `Commits:` names the commits whose prose is
   being corrected. The `git log --grep '^Docs:'` branch-range walk and the
   `Overview:` parameter are gone. `stages/execute.md` writes the dispatch
   template once, in the per-task loop, and every later site names that template.

3. The end-of-plan gate loses its documenter step and is now Format, Check, Unit
   tests, then the e2e and sanity runs; the repair routing that pointed at the
   deleted step now names the documenter template in its `Fix scope:` shape. The
   invariant — a prose pass follows every commit that changes code, scoped to
   that commit — is applied at the per-task fix commit, the gate repair commit,
   and the acceptance-blocker fix commit, and a repair that changed no documented
   code draws none. Per-task defect routing splits by kind, code first so no fix
   ships undocumented, and the reviewer now tags every defect prose or not-prose
   so the orchestrator routes without guessing.

4. The reviewer verifies the recorded checklist answers instead of re-deriving
   them: answers are read as the union across the task's commits, `pass` is
   spot-checked where the diff can confirm it, and only rules every commit
   answers `n-a` earn an independent derivation. Acceptance locates those answers
   by `Task <ID>:` commit and narrows its `## Prose` sweep to the `Docs:` commits
   no reviewer saw, discriminated by progress-log heading.

Verification is the Test exception for guidance markdown: Format, Check and the
full unit suite are green, and the substitute dry-run walkthrough traces a
two-pass run end to end against the edited text — implementer entry and commit,
documenter dispatch and scope, reviewer commits and union read, both defect
routes, the gate, both repair kinds, and acceptance's two sweeps.

Checklist: 1 pass — markdown-only diff, grep of added lines finds no print/console/debugger or commented-out code · 2 n-a — no new files; six existing instruction files edited · 3 pass — grep of added lines finds no `REQ-` identifier · 4 pass — the diff's file list is exactly the task's six files plus the progress log · 5 n-a — the task cites the config's Test exception for guidance markdown, verified by the dry-run walkthrough instead · 6 n-a — the diff adds no code comments, only instruction prose
